rows.label: Share of the Sierra Club Foundation's programme grants outside Beyond Coal that fund climate and clean-energy work

source.title: Sierra Club, Form 990 for 2024 (IRS e-file XML, object 202503169349309600), Schedule O, Part III line 4a
source.quote: THE SIERRA CLUB FOUNDATION, GRANTS US 501(C)(3) FUNDING FOR OUR MOST IMPACTFUL CAMPAIGNS TO PROTECT WILDLANDS, TRANSFORM THE ENERGY SECTOR, PUBLIC EDUCATION, AND ADMINISTRATIVE ADVOCACY.

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both charityevals models of the Foundation so the split is one set of numbers. The Foundation's Form 990 names Beyond Coal as a programme; the rest of its grants (the Chapter and Group Education Project, the National Education Project and 'additional grants', 98.5% of them to the Sierra Club) are not split by campaign. Anchor: the Sierra Club's account of 2024 (Form 990, Schedule O) gives about half its campaign space to climate and energy (Beyond Dirty Fuels' gas pipelines and export terminals, Clean Transportation for All, industrial transformation, EPA's power-plant standards) and half to lands and waters, outdoors for all, species and clean air and water; its chapters work on both. 50% (35% to 65%).

rows.label: The Sierra Club Foundation's share of the resources behind the Sierra Club's climate, lands and clean-air campaigns

source.title: The Sierra Club Foundation, Form 990 for 2024 (IRS e-file XML, object 202502689349300025), Schedule I; Sierra Club, Form 990 for 2024 (object 202503169349309600), Part I line 18
source.note: Schedule I: grant to the Sierra Club $85,639,241 for 2024 (98.5% of the Foundation's grants of $86,925,218); the Sierra Club's total expenses for 2024 were $171,800,410 (its Form 990, Part I line 18, at the second URL, 2025_TEOS_XML_11A.zip).

rows.explainer: The Foundation's grants pay for the charitable part of the Sierra Club's work; the Sierra Club (a 501(c)(4)) adds its own money (membership dues, lobbying and electoral funds). The Foundation's $85.6M was half of the Sierra Club's $171.8M of spending in 2024, but much of the rest is membership, the magazine, outings fees and lobbying; the administrative advocacy, litigation and public education that won the counted rules and coal closings are the charitable work the Foundation funds (Beyond Coal is a programme of the Foundation's own Form 990). A closer anchor: the Sierra Club's 2024 conservation campaigns cost $83.9M (its Form 990, Part III line 4a), and the Foundation's grants less its chapter and national education projects came to about $61M, about 73% of that. Our judgment, 70% (50%, the overall ratio, to 90%) of the Sierra Club's resources behind these campaigns, so that each model credits the Foundation with that part of the Sierra Club's share of a win; the Sierra Club's own money is among the others' resources (templates.md Convention 2).
